testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If there is ice on your side mirror, what does this mean?

options.text: You should leave the road.
The road is likely icy too.
The road will not be icy.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is likely icy too.
questions.explanation: If your mirrors or wipers are icy, the road surface is probably icy as well.

questions.question: What should you do if the low air pressure warning light comes on?

options.text: Keep driving and repair the brakes within a week.
Pull over and check the brakes right away.
Call a mechanic while you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the brakes right away.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop the vehicle safely while you can still control the brakes. Check and fix the brakes as soon as possible.

questions.question: What should you do if your engine catches fire?

options.text: Open the hood right away.
Turn off the engine right away.
Do not use a fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine right away.
questions.explanation: To stop an engine fire from spreading, turn off the engine immediately. Do not open the hood unless you have to.

questions.question: What color is the warning light for an ABS problem?

options.text: Green
Yellow
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: ABS warning lights are yellow. If the ABS is not working, you can still use the regular braking system.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you in a large vehicle, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Slow down gradually.
Leave more space between you and the car ahead.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, slow down gradually and increase your distance from the car ahead. Speeding up will only make the tailgater follow at a higher speed.

questions.question: When placing warning triangles on the road, how should you hold them?

options.text: Between your body and the oncoming traffic.
Behind your back so other drivers cannot see them.
As low to the ground as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between your body and the oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: For your safety, hold the warning triangles between you and the oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What will you do during the vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Change a tire.
Explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.
Guess the weight of a trailer load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your whole vehicle. You will explain each part you check and why you are checking it.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Slow down.
Speed up.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, reduce your speed.

questions.question: A driver with an open window in cold weather may be:

options.text: Distracted or impaired.
Dressed too warmly.
Someone who likes fresh air.

questions.correctAnswerText: Distracted or impaired.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs that a driver may be impaired. Drivers who are drunk, tired, on drugs, or sick can be dangerous. One sign is having the window down in cold weather.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the wheel hard.
Do not use the brakes.
Put the vehicle in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not brake. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This will help you regain grip on the road.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With both hands.
With one hand to keep the other hand free.
With one hand at a time, switching between hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: When do skids happen?

options.text: When tires lose grip on the road.
When there is too much weight in the trailer.
When ABS activates.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tires lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: Skids happen when tires lose traction with the road. This can happen from hard braking, hard acceleration, sharp turns, or driving too fast.

questions.question: What should you do before trying to put out an engine fire?

options.text: Open the hood.
Turn off the engine.
Press the accelerator to use up remaining fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine.
questions.explanation: If there is an engine fire, turn off the engine right away. Do not open the hood when putting out the fire.

questions.question: Why is backing toward the driver's side recommended when backing with a trailer?

options.text: The driver has the best view.
Power lines should be on the passenger's side.
Other drivers can help on the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver has the best view.
questions.explanation: When backing up, turn toward the left side. This gives the driver the best view of the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: What is blocking a load?

options.text: Dangerous and should never be done.
Important to keep cargo from moving during transport.
Only done with liquid cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Important to keep cargo from moving during transport.
questions.explanation: Block cargo to prevent it from sliding during transport. Shifting cargo can make steering and handling harder for the driver.

questions.question: What is Gross Combination Weight?

options.text: The total weight of the truck, trailer, and cargo.
The total weight of a single vehicle without cargo.
The maximum weight allowed by the manufacturer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of the truck, trailer, and cargo.
questions.explanation: Gross Combination Weight (GCW) is the total weight of a truck, its trailer(s), and all cargo.

questions.question: You should be able to stop within:

options.text: 10 feet of your vehicle.
100 feet of your vehicle.
The distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must be able to stop within the distance you can see. Slow down when you cannot see far ahead.

questions.question: You should not use your mirrors to:

options.text: Change lanes.
Make a turn.
Check how fast you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how fast you are going.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when changing lanes, turning, merging, and making tight maneuvers. Do not use mirrors to check your speed.

questions.question: Drivers talking to passengers should be viewed as:

options.text: Responsible drivers.
Distracted drivers.
Knowledgeable drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Distracted drivers.
questions.explanation: Drivers talking to passengers may be distracted from driving. Be careful around distracted drivers.

questions.question: If your mirrors are dirty before you start driving:

options.text: They will become clean after a short drive.
It is not a problem.
Clean them before you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clean them before you drive.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check your mirrors and windshield for dirt. Clean them so you can see clearly.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can be used for:

options.text: Making the air brakes work more effectively.
Temporarily releasing the spring brakes.
Charging the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Temporarily releasing the spring brakes.
questions.explanation: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they are activated due to low air pressure. Pushing the correct control will release the spring brakes for a short time. This lets the driver move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Can damage parts of a vehicle.
Is necessary to warm up parts of a vehicle.
Is encouraged to improve a vehicle's gas mileage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can damage parts of a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always speed up smoothly and gradually. Do not jerk your vehicle. Rough acceleration can cause damage to the engine and other parts.

questions.question: Cargo inside a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be secured.
Should be stacked no more than three feet high.
Should be secured to prevent movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be secured to prevent movement.
questions.explanation: All cargo in a trailer must be secured properly. This prevents it from shifting during travel.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the safe operation of a vehicle?

options.text: The driver
The mechanic
The owner

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for safe vehicle operation. Always perform routine vehicle inspections before driving a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle?

options.text: 3 psi in one minute.
6 psi in one minute.
8 psi in one minute.

questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute.
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a double combination vehicle with air brakes, air should leak no faster than 3 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, do not drive the vehicle. Something needs repair.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Only use the side mirrors on the driver's side.
Use both side mirrors.
Never use a helper.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Backing a commercial motor vehicle is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Check both side mirrors frequently when backing. Use a helper whenever possible.

questions.question: The radiator cap:

options.text: Should not be removed when the coolant is hot.
Can be removed when the coolant is hot.
Should be cool to the touch under normal driving conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be removed when the coolant is hot.
questions.explanation: Never remove the radiator cap or any pressurized cooling system part until it cools down. Opening a hot cap can release steam and boiling water that can severely burn you. If the cap is cool to the touch, the system is safe to open.

questions.question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact to better communicate with them.
Ignore their gestures.
Not move out of their path of travel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore their gestures.
questions.explanation: If confronted by an aggressive driver, move out of their way if possible. Do not make eye contact, as this can provoke them. Do not let their actions provoke you.

questions.question: If a vehicle begins to hydroplane, the driver should:

options.text: Accelerate.
Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
Pull in the clutch and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This helps you regain control.

questions.question: Using the brakes creates heat. If too much heat is produced:

options.text: The brakes may not work.
The brakes may squeak more than usual.
The brakes will brake unevenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may not work.
questions.explanation: Brakes are designed to handle a lot of heat, but do not rely only on brakes to slow your vehicle. If brakes get too hot, they may fade and lose stopping power. Also use engine braking.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should:

options.text: Be done the same way every time.
Be done differently every time.
Not always include all items to check.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be done the same way every time.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you remember all the steps and prevents you from missing anything.

questions.question: When braking on dry pavement at 55 mph, how much distance does brake lag add to your stopping distance?

options.text: 32 feet
45 feet
20 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 32 feet
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: If you hear an unusual noise or feel something strange while driving, you should:

options.text: Ignore it and keep driving.
Hope the vehicle lasts until another driver takes over.
Stop and check it to find the problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check it to find the problem.
questions.explanation: Pay attention to what you see, hear, smell, or feel while driving. If anything seems wrong, stop and check it out.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with power steering, check that:

options.text: The fluid level is correct.
The hoses are connected to the battery.
Any leak is small.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fluid level is correct.
questions.explanation: Check the hoses, pumps, and fluid level on power steering systems. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: To put out an electrical fire, you should use:

options.text: Water.
A B:C extinguisher.
An X extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: A B:C extinguisher.
questions.explanation: B:C fire extinguishers work on electrical fires and burning liquids. Never use water on an electrical fire.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator in an air brake system:

options.text: Makes brakes work without squeaking.
Stops ice from forming in the braking system.
Lubricates braking system parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops ice from forming in the braking system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an evaporator that adds alcohol to the system. The alcohol prevents ice from forming.

questions.question: A bridge formula:

options.text: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.
Allows more weight for trucks.
Is not important for drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.
questions.explanation: A bridge formula sets the maximum weight allowed on each axle. Axles that are close together have a lower maximum weight limit.

questions.question: Placards for hazardous cargo must be placed:

options.text: Only on the front of the vehicle.
On the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle.
Only on the driver's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Placards must be on the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle. They must be visible from all directions.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, you should:

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
Not worry about how weight is distributed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
questions.explanation: Each axle must have the correct weight. Too little or too much weight can cause steering problems, reduce traction, or damage the axles.

questions.question: When you start an engine, oil pressure should reach normal level:

options.text: Within seconds.
Within five minutes.
After about three minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within seconds.
questions.explanation: Check your gauges when the engine starts. Oil pressure should reach normal level within seconds.

questions.question: If you plan to transport hazardous materials, you will:

options.text: Need to get a hazardous materials endorsement.
Need to drive with flashing lights on.
Need to wear a gas mask.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to get a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a hazardous materials endorsement to transport hazardous materials that require the vehicle to have warning placards.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, you must maintain ____ with your vehicle at all times.

options.text: Three points of contact
Four points of contact
Two points of contact

questions.correctAnswerText: Three points of contact
questions.explanation: Face the vehicle and keep three points of contact as you exit. If the vehicle is a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: Alcohol evaporators are:

options.text: Illegal.
Devices that add alcohol to air brake systems.
Only allowed in the northern parts of the state.

questions.correctAnswerText: Devices that add alcohol to air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have alcohol evaporators. They add alcohol to the braking system to help prevent ice from forming.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer
The maximum weight a vehicle can pull
The minimum weight a vehicle must haul

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer
questions.explanation: The Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum loaded weight for a single vehicle as set by the manufacturer.

questions.question: To avoid a collision with a hazard on the road:

options.text: You should always try to stop.
Swerving may be safer than stopping.
You should never swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be safer than stopping.
questions.explanation: Sometimes swerving is safer than stopping. You can turn away from a hazard faster than you can come to a complete stop.

questions.question: What is the number one cause of death and injury in a work zone?

options.text: Drivers speeding
Slow drivers
Animals crossing the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers speeding
questions.explanation: Speeding is the leading cause of death and injury in work zones. Drive slowly and carefully around workers.

questions.question: What is a drawback of retarders?

options.text: They may not be allowed everywhere.
They help slow a vehicle.
They cannot be turned off.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not be allowed everywhere.
questions.explanation: A retarder slows a vehicle and reduces brake use. However, retarders can be noisy and are not permitted in all places.

questions.question: When starting a vehicle, the oil pressure should:

options.text: Gradually build up over a few minutes.
Reach normal level within a few seconds.
Start high, then decrease as the engine runs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reach normal level within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal within seconds of starting the engine.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Continue driving and finish your trip.
Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Safely pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you become drowsy, stop and sleep. Driving while tired causes many serious accidents. Do not try to push through and finish your trip.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, the heaviest cargo should be placed:

options.text: On top of lighter cargo.
Under lighter cargo.
At the rear of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under lighter cargo.
questions.explanation: Avoid making vehicles top-heavy. Top-heavy vehicles are more likely to roll over. Place heavy cargo under lighter cargo.
